what_this_session_was_for: Session one proved that run() EXECUTES on Kaggle and self-terminates gracefully, but it was the FIRST link and therefore had nothing to resume from -- seed_checkpoints() ran on an empty input and correctly seeded zero in silence. So the chain's load-bearing property was still untested: whether a later session READS the prior link's epochs rather than recomputing them. If it recomputes, the chain is not a chain, it is five independent 4-epoch runs and the arm can never finish. This session tested exactly that, at the plan's full 8.0 h ceiling rather than session one's deliberately short 1.0 h.
headline: RESUME IS DEMONSTRATED. The chain accumulates, and four seeds now stand complete at the frozen 7-epoch budget.

resume_is_now_PROVEN_and_by_two_independ.route_1_the_reconciler: epochs_added_by_this_link = 29 against previous_total_epochs = 4, for a total of 33. Had the session recomputed seed 0's four epochs, the added count would have been 33 and the total 33 -- the two routes would agree numerically while describing different worlds, which is why the reconciler reports the DELTA and the prior total separately rather than only the total.
resume_is_now_PROVEN_and_by_two_independ.route_2_the_kernel_log_itself: Two lines, neither derived from the reconciler: `seeded 2 prior checkpoint file(s) for the BAKED dataset /kaggle/input/ft-ckpt-s1 (searched /kaggle/input); found in: /kaggle/input/datasets/emanueleebrahimi/ft-ckpt-s1` at t=50.3 s, then `seed 0: resuming at epoch 4 (4 recorded)` at t=1417.0 s. The session read the dataset, found two files, and entered seed 0 at epoch 5 rather than epoch 1.
resume_is_now_PROVEN_and_by_two_independ.why_two_routes_matter_here: The reconciler is MY code and it passed vacuously once already on session one's record (it read a top-level `seeds` key that run() does not write). A property this load-bearing should not rest on the instrument that has already failed at this exact task. The log is written by the kernel, parsed by nothing, and says the same thing.
resume_is_now_PROVEN_and_by_two_independ.the_baked_path_was_WRONG_AGAIN_and_the_f: The baked hint `/kaggle/input/ft-ckpt-s1` did not exist; the recursive INPUT_ROOT search found the real mount at `/kaggle/input/datasets/emanueleebrahimi/ft-ckpt-s1`. This is the SECOND consecutive session in which the predicted mount path was wrong and the fallback saved the run -- which retrospectively justifies the Step 5 decision NOT to bake the now-known path, because baking it would have re-introduced the prediction that has now failed twice.

measured_result_SCOPED.DO_NOT_COMPARE_THIS_TO_THE_COMPARATOR_YE: The comparator is 0.5076, the MEDIAN over TEN seeds of the frozen-embedding arm at split_frac 0.25. Three of session one's four objections are UNCHANGED and remain disqualifying: it is four seeds not ten; ZERO of the three required shuffled-label nulls have run and the null is a GATE in the frozen bar, so nothing yet bounds how much of this is a random readout of an already-informative representation; and the bar's verdict is a PAIRED BOOTSTRAP against the committed per-seed comparator values, which needs all ten. One objection HAS been discharged -- these four seeds each reached their full 7-epoch budget, so frozen_budget.value is no longer computed over a truncated curve. The arm's status is still `planned` and its ceiling_verdict still `blocked:untried-arm`, correctly.
measured_result_SCOPED.what_it_IS_evidence_for: Four INDEPENDENT seeds each ran their full frozen budget and all four landed in a narrow band, 0.6307 to 0.6879, a spread of 0.0572. Every one of them starts from an untrained baseline near or below zero (-0.153 to +0.0968) and rises monotonically-ish to the 0.63-0.69 band. That the band is narrow across four seeds is a reproducibility result about the TRAINING PROCEDURE, not a verdict about the arm. It is also, for the first time in this arm, a number that could in principle be compared to 0.5076 -- it simply cannot be compared yet, because the null gate has not run.

the_rate_RE_MEASURED_and_session_ones_fi.what: Session one's artifact ended with an explicit instruction: `Re-read the logs rather than quoting 923.6 s`, because that figure rested on THREE steady-state epochs of ONE seed in ONE session. Re-read, it was low.
the_rate_RE_MEASURED_and_session_ones_fi.session_2_encode_bearing_basis: 4 seed-openings (seeds 1-4); seed 0's opening epoch belongs to session one
the_rate_RE_MEASURED_and_session_ones_fi.why_the_in_session_measurement_is_STILL_: 1323.3 s is again a ONE-EPOCH cold figure carrying CUDA context setup and the initial tile encoding, exactly as the smoke's 1276.7 s was. It overstates this session's own steady state by 33.7%. The measurement is not wrong; it answers `how long does a cold epoch take` and is being read as `how long does an epoch take`. That is the same measurement-SHAPE error the session-one artifact named, and it recurs every session because the routine is unchanged.
the_rate_RE_MEASURED_and_session_ones_fi.how_much_to_trust_990: Far more than 923.6. It is 25 epochs across 5 independent seeds on one device, and the within-session spread is tight (955-1029, a 7.8% band). The residual risk is that it is still ONE session on ONE T4 instance, and Kaggle T4s are not identical; session three re-measures it again.

the_schedule_REBUILT_from_this_session.method: Two independent derivations, deliberately. The first uses only the QUOTA LEDGER and assumes nothing about epoch structure; the second builds from the per-epoch model. They agree to within 0.1%, which is the check.

derivation_1_quota_only.how_derived: quota went 1.86 h -> 10.43 h across the session, and no other GPU session ran in that window
derivation_1_quota_only.note: This figure absorbs pre-run overhead, the throwaway rate epoch, the encode-bearing openings, steady state and the boundary overshoot, all of it. It is the only rate that needs no model.

derivation_2_per_epoch_model.the_null_assumption_named: The three nulls are costed at the same 1176 + 6x990 shape as a real seed. A shuffled-label null trains the same architecture on the same tensor shapes, so this should hold -- but it has never been measured on this device and is an ASSUMPTION, not a measurement.

the_schedule_REBUILT_from_this_session.epochs_remaining_breakdown: seed 4 needs 2; seeds 5-9 need 7 each = 35; three nulls need 7 each = 21
the_schedule_REBUILT_from_this_session.verdict: THE GRADEABLE PREFIX STILL FITS INSIDE THIS QUOTA WEEK, with roughly 2.4 h of margin -- down from the 4 h that session one projected, because the rate is 7.2% higher than that projection assumed.
the_schedule_REBUILT_from_this_session.the_margin_is_THINNER_than_it_was_and_th: Session one resolved the plan's top risk NEGATIVE with ~4 h of slack. One more 7% rate drift would take the need to ~18.3 h against 19.57 h, leaving ~1.2 h -- still fitting, but no longer comfortably. The risk is not re-opened; it is narrowed. If session three's re-measured rate drifts up again, re-derive before pushing session four rather than assuming this week still holds.

cost.wall_vs_ceiling: The session's own run clock reports 30828 s of advance() time against a 28800 s ceiling, so it overshot its deadline by 2028 s -- about two epochs rather than session one's partial one, because at 990 s/epoch the deadline fell early in a pair of in-flight epochs across the seed-4 boundary. The practical rule from session one (`ceiling + 0.36 h + up to one epoch`) UNDERSTATES this; the overshoot is bounded by one epoch PER PHASE BOUNDARY crossed, not one per session.
cost.redundant_cost_recurred_as_predicted: The in-session rate-measurement epoch cost 1323.3 s (0.368 h) and changed no behaviour, the horizon having been supplied. That is the ~21 min/session redundancy identified before session one and deliberately left in place. Over the two sessions run so far it has cost 0.723 h; over the two remaining it will cost ~0.74 h more, which is 30% of the remaining 2.4 h margin. If the margin becomes binding, THIS is the first thing to cut -- it is a known-safe deletion and the only reason it survived was that it sat immediately before run()'s first-ever execution, which is no longer the situation.

defects_found_this_session.none_in_my_own_code: The reconciler, rebuilt after session one's vacuity defect, read `per_seed` correctly, compared 5 record-side seeds against 5 disk curves, found zero mismatches, and reported `n_record_seeds_compared: 5` so the non-vacuity is visible in the output rather than assumed. The both-directions check found no disk curve the record failed to mention. This is the first time that instrument has done real work.
defects_found_this_session.one_plan_level_observation: `top_level_bounded_field_present` is again `false`, as expected -- the plan's Verification item 5 names a field that does not exist. The property is recorded twice at the run level (`status` and `phases[0].bounded_here`) and both are present. Unchanged from session one; recorded so the absence does not read as a new problem.

honest_limits: Four seeds of ten and ZERO of the three required nulls. Nothing here is a result about the arm, and the ledger correctly still reads `planned` / `blocked:untried-arm`. The null is a gate, not a formality.
The 0.6505 median is over four seeds. The comparator's 0.5076 is over ten. Medians over different n are not two estimates of one quantity.
The 990.0 s rate is one session on one T4 instance. It is much better powered than session one's 923.6 but is not a device-independent constant; Kaggle T4 instances vary.
The three nulls' cost is modelled on the real seeds' shape and has never been measured.
The schedule's 2.4 h margin assumes the rate does not drift further. It drifted +7.2% between sessions one and two.

Seed 3 has both the highest untrained baseline (+0.0968) and the highest final value (0.6879), and seed 2 has the lowest of each (-0.153, 0.6307). With n=4 that is a coincidence worth noticing and nothing more -- do NOT report it as a relationship.
